title: Mayor Mamdani to meet with President Trump in NYC on Monday | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will meet with President Donald Trump on Monday ahead of the United Nations General Assembly, Mamdani’s office said Sunday.

The meeting will take place at Gracie Mansion, the mayoral residence in Manhattan, marking the first time Trump will meet with Mamdani on his home turf.

A spokesperson for Mamdani said the meeting would “focus on issues affecting New York City and New Yorkers.”

Trump is scheduled to speak at the UN General Assembly in the city on Tuesday. The White House confirmed the meeting with the mayor but did not offer additional details.

Monday will mark the third time Mamdani and Trump have met in person. Their first meeting was held in the Oval Officein November 2025, shortly after Mamdani’s election, followed by a second meetingin February.

Mamdani has said when he speaks with Trump, it’s always focused on the needs of the city.

“When it comes to the president, we continue to have a conversation about how best to deliver for this city,” he told reporters. “That is a conversation that has been done in person, it’s been done over the phone, and it will continue so long as either of us have the ability to deliver for the city.”

Despite their opposing politics, Trump and Mamdani have had surprisingly amiable meetings. Staffers for Mamdani argue the mayor has chosen a diplomatic approach with the president, which has proved advantageous for the city. New York has been spared from the large-scale immigration enforcement Trump threatened during the mayoral campaign and, despite threats that he would “take over,” the president has been surprisingly complimentary of Mamdani’s stewardship of his hometown.

The mayor’s staffers declined to say exactly what Trump and Mamdani will discuss, but the president’s immigration agenda has been a consistent pressure point. Just last week,Mamdani announced a lawsuitagainst the Trump administration over its expansion of a rule that would make it harder for some immigrants to get green cards.

While Mamdani and Trump are ideologically opposed, the mayor’s aides point to concrete outcomes from his previous discussions with Trump as evidence that the meetings are politically favorable.

During the February gathering, Mamdani demanded the release of Elmina Aghayeva, a Columbia University student who wasdetained by federal immigrationagents inside her university residence. After meeting with the president, Mamdani said Trump called him to inform him Aghayeva would be released.

During that same meeting, Mamdani pitched Trump on a massive housing project in Queens that would require billions in federal grants. The mayor brought visual props to make his case for what could be the biggest federal investment in housing in 50 years, including a mock-up of a New York Daily News front page bearing the president’s face and the headline: “Trump to City: Let’s Build.”

While no progress has been made on the project, aides to Mamdani said both parties agreed to continue discussions.

Monday’s meeting also gives Mamdani an unusually prominent spot on the international stage. With world leaders and journalists gathered in New York for the UN General Assembly, the encounter at the mayor’s residence is likely to draw significant attention beyond the city.

Mamdani’s aides say the mayor’s ability to keep his policy differences from the president while also extracting commitments is evidence that maintaining a relationship with Trump can produce results for New York. Whether that approach continues to produce results will be closely watched after Monday’s meeting.

Trump has referred to Mamdani as “my little communist” and has tried to use the mayor, a democratic socialist, as a foil, linking his politics to Democrats across the country. During his campaign, Mamdani said he would “become Donald Trump’s worst nightmare.”

Despite the rhetoric, Trump also referred to Mamdani as a “very rational person” and said he was “very comfortable” with the mayor running New York City following their first Oval Office meeting.

“The better he does, the happier I am. I will say there’s no difference in party. There’s no difference in anything, and we’re going to be helping him to make everybody’s dream come true — having a strong and very safe New York,” Trump said after the meeting.

Presidential visits to New York City’s mayoral residence are rare. Presidentialrecordsshow the last president to visit was Ronald Reagan, who visited Gracie Mansion and presented then-Mayor Ed Koch with a prop check as a sign of the Reagan administration’s commitment to an infrastructure project in Manhattan.

President John F. KennedyvisitedGracie Mansion in 1962 to delivera speech on medical care before a group of US mayors. President Jimmy Carter and first lady Rosalynn Carter were overnight guests at the mansion in 1978. Carter made the visit during anofficialtrip to New York City and a bill signing ceremony at City Hall alongside Koch.

The Monday meeting at the mayor’s residence also comes days before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is scheduled to address the United Nations on Thursday. Mamdani, anardent criticof the Israeli government, has said he does not plan to participate in any planned demonstrations against Netanyahu.

This story has been updated with additional information.
